text:
sarah: CI job started failing this morning on prod runner — helm upgrade --install errors out with 403 when server-side applying the release. logs show: 
```
ERROR: api-server: 403 Forbidden: service account "project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" cannot impersonate requested principal
```
I think this started after kube-runner image bump yesterday. Anyone seen impersonation / workload-identity issues?

morgan: can you paste the full job log? which cluster and namespace?

sarah: cluster: gke-prod-1, namespace: infra-ci, runner: gitlab-runner-5. Short log: 
```
kubectl apply -f release.yaml --server-side
Error from server (Forbidden): releases.helm.sh "webapp" is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:infra-ci:ci-runner" cannot impersonate serviceaccount "project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```
No explicit SA key used, we rely on Workload Identity. annotation on CI k8s SA is present: `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

oncall-bot: @sarah thanks for filing. Escalating to eng-sre if not resolved in 30m.

raj: quick checklist: 1) confirm IAM binding: the GCP SA needs `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` binding for the K8s service account identity (member = "serviceAccount:PROJECT.svc.id.goog[namespace/sa]"). 2) check token audience and token TTL mismatch. 3) confirm no accidental IAM policy denial on project/folder.

morgan: can you run this to check binding?
```
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod
```

sarah: ran it, policy doesn't list any `serviceAccount:PROJECT.svc.id.goog[infra-ci/ci-runner]`. So the WI binding is missing. Not sure why it vanished.

raj: that explains it — without that binding, the token exchange fails and impersonation is denied. To fix: add the policy binding: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser \
  --member "serviceAccount:redwood-prod.svc.id.goog[infra-ci/ci-runner]" \
  --project=redwood-prod
```
Then ensure the k8s SA still has the annotation `iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: project-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and restart the pod / runner so node token is refreshed.

sarah: applied the binding and restarted the runner pod. re-ran pipeline — helm release still failing but different error now: token TTL too long? logs: `audience mismatch` in OAuth exchange.

morgan: did the annotation accidentally include a typo or extra space? also check the identity namespace in the member string — sometimes our PROJECT var is wrong on CI images.

raj: also check runner config: `GITLAB_RUNNER_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROJECT` env we recently introduced. If the audience in the OIDC token doesn't match the SA expected audience, GKE rejects. On older runners we set audience to `https://iam.googleapis.com/token`. New ones expect `identitynamespace:PROJECT.svc.id.goog`.

sarah: aha — our runner env is still setting audience to the legacy URL. quick patch to runner config to set `GCP_OIDC_TOKEN_AUDIENCE=redwood-prod.svc.id.goog` then restarted, re-run pipeline.

devops-bot: ping: created a short-lived fallback key and stored in Vault path `kv/ci/project-sa/fallback` for immediate unblock (expiry 1h). Not recommended long-term.

sarah: pipeline now passes, helm release applied :party_parrot: Looks like root cause = accidental deletion of the workloadIdentityUser binding combined with a mismatch in token audience on upgraded runner image.

morgan: TL;DR and action items: 1) re-add binding (done), 2) update runner image/env to set correct audience (blocked commit open -> PR #422), 3) add an IAM policy monitor alert if WI bindings for critical SAs change. I'll open follow-ups.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved. Severity: P2. Time to recover ~42 minutes. Documenting steps in internal runbook (link).

sarah: thanks all — leaving the fallback key expiry as-is. Will check vault audit logs later to verify no use after this incident.
